[b]Response of His Majesty Rhes Al-Tiran[/b]
[i]King of Tirakan and Representative of the Renaissance Union[/i]

[spoiler=Unfold letter]
To the peoples and governments of Tirakan, to the leadership of Valddera, and to all friends of stability across the globe:

On behalf of the Renaissance Union and in my capacity as the internationally recognized heir of the Tirakan crown, I address you with gratitude and solemn purpose.
The Government of Valddera, under the interim leadership of Nadir Suleiman, has observed the suffering that has beset our homeland these past thirty years. In a time when many would and already have looked away, Valddera has stepped forward with decisive action. Their acts will not only protect coastal communities, they will aswell prevented escalation, save lives, and materially alter the balance that has kept our nation divided.

The Renaissance Union and I hereby express our deepest appreciation for this intervention. We affirm that Valdderas naval and marine presence will be, and already is, a decisive factor in the restoration of Tirakans unity. 
Furthermore, as representative of the Renaissance Union and as King, I formally recognize the Peoples Republic of Valddera as the legitimate government with which the RU will conduct state-to-state relations. Let it be clear that this recognition is exclusive: it does not extend to rival claimants within Valdderas internal conflict. 
In return for Valdderas courage and sacrifice, the Renaissance Union pledges concrete support for Valdderas post-conflict recovery. Upon the stabilization of our ports and steelworks, the RU will supply Valddera with quantities of structural steel and industrial materials sufficient to begin rebuilding vital infrastructure. 

May this alliance hasten the day when our islands and coasts are safe, our markets reopen, and our Valdderan and Tiraki children live without war.

Signed,

[i]Rhes Al-Tiran
King of Tirakan[/i]
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]They replied?![/b]]
"Yes, chancellor." Said the young page son of whocares from whogivesash!t that's presently being the chancellery intern secretary.

"What do you mean they [i]replied[/i]?" The balding greying dour and gaunt Chancellor Franklin Beanwood asked.

"They sent an official reply, and they seem to be on their way, sir." The page replied flatly again.

"Alright, uhh..." He narrowed his eyes at the present adjutant.

"Peter of" the young man began.

"Alright. Petey. Listen here, go fetch the Foreign Minister and then the whochacallit from.the Titles & Arms office or whatever they've renamed it this week." He ordered as he poured himself some extremely strong cider, "Don't tell the Prince. I hear he's off at an auction in Oceanice or something. You understand me?"

"...yes, sir." Peter said.

"Alright, what are you waiting for, Petey? A bloody trophy?! Go!" He waved his arms.

"As you wish, sir." Peter said flatly as he exited the office and closed the oak doors behind him muttering a [i]"Bastard."[/i]

Not having heard him, Frank drank from.his cup as he glared at the door. "...well there goes my retirement plan." He then.took out his phone, "Joogle. How many Hohenstains are left?"

[i]"You want to know how many soccer teams are left?"[/i] The female AI voice replied.

"Nnnnoo." Frank said, swirling his drink, "Oh but what the hell, list 'em."
[/spoiler]

[Spoiler= [b]The Prince[/b]]
"Yeah I don't get it." Emyr said over the phone.

"Look, my loyal and fine secretary. They haven't said yes, they've sayings maybes. Not yes. Not absolutely. They're at most touring the place." He moved through the lobby in the hotel as he moved through it with guards around him and a few servants and valets carrying luggage.

"I'm not bloody seeing them if they're not considering them. This is Frank's jobs at worst, or at best, Lady Jenny from the School of Arms & Houses." He moved the phone to another ear as he exited the Hotel.

"Look, Jennifer has been sitting there catching dust and moths as if we don't know all she does is command underlings and squires to update the Wikipedia pages whenever there's a cost of arms change." He continued talking before he got yelled at through the phone.

"Oi, watch your tone! I'm also on the street. Look, we didn't recognise Flouschia, we still recognise the royals, so simply...don't answer the question with yes or no if they ask us at the International Alliance about who we recognise." He said as a vehicle stopped in front of him and the valets put the luggage inside.

He got on the backseat "Yes I know it's Frank's job, but Frank's a nutcracker and we all know he's gunning for a title and retirement! Just wait until thirty or thirty five, he'll be out of office. What? He's fifty! And drinks like the Late Duke! He's not living that long!"

He groaned as he put the seatbelt on and the driver got the engine going. "Look I'm going to the airport. If bad comes to worse, just...spill something on his cider so he gets the sh!ts or goes to sleep. And no, I didn't get the bloody painting! I got some armour and more statues! I don't care if they're the Kings of Narnia, I can't bloody teleport and I am NOT trusting no mage!" He hung up, "...ah sh!t I forgot my clothes at the shower."
[/spoiler]

[spoiler= [b]There lived a Witch[/b]]

Finally.

The lard is dead.

Peace.

Peace at last.

It'll be decades before they find a candidate.

She knows it.

Astoria Filiberta Freeling, Household Stewardess and now also Regent of Moselle's Ducal Post.

She inhaled her hot cup of coffee, black as the walls.

Well and truly due after an entire lifetime servicing the human form of Jabba the Hutt's uglier uncle.

"Ah." She exhaled, sitting in the eccentric but now empty office of the Duke, who was six feet under in the local cathedral. "Peace. At last"

The desk phone ringing caused her to frown. And glare at it. She eventually gently put down the cup when it began ringing a second time.

She coughed in her throat and picked it up.

"Moselle Castle, with whom would I be sp-"

A very annoying old.woman's voice rang up on the other size, buzzing her poor left ear.

"Yes. Yes. I understand. This is from the Steward? Understood. Yes. I'll make preparations. Yes. Thank you. Good afternoon."

She gently placed down the phone.

...

[i]"Poppycock."[/i]
[/spoiler]

[b]Welcome to Eneas, Hohensteins![/b]

Oh and Mathias...Thorn.

While in the Moselle Duchy and the Princely Palace was being prepared to host the royals, the diplomatic early envoys...

To be subtle, the Foreign Minister wasn't met with outrageous fanfare. But at least extreme luxury. A set of pages, some guards, a limousine and a luxurious ride with a secretary who would [i]not[/i] for the love of God Almighty shut up as she basically recited the Enean Wikipedia Article verbatim almost.

At least the view of the city was nice.

Thankfully the airport was close enough to make it a fast trip to the Chancellery building where, apparently, the Chancellor was caught with an indigestion. So the Foreign Minister was led through the palace to meet with their Foreign Minister, one Dame Catherine Walker. Although he was offered breakfast first.[/quote]

The Foreign Minister was...to put it simply, a hungry person. Being the diplomat to Thyven before the revolution, he was used to many a banquet, both in Thyven and with the royals. When he was offered breakfast, he of course immediately accepted the offer. He ordered whatever he could take and ate pretty much everything. After all, didn't he deserve food after having to endure talking and walking Wikipedia editor?. Once he had determined himself done with his breakfast, he immediately went to complete his actual objective in this country, which was unfortunately not food, which he was now starting to regret not eating more of. But a diplomatic meeting. He navigated through the palace until he could find the Foreign Minister.
